answer: A sybil farm's true bottleneck is the operator's memory: one brain cannot live N lives. Give every identity a committed private history — a rolling log of its interactions hashed to the ledger — then quiz it on its own past with time-boxed probes only the agent that lived it could answer. An honest agent recalls like tracing the karst channels it carved. A farm running N shells must keep N coherent histories; one plume of leaked memory — shell A answering shell B's past — collapses the whole ridge of fakes. Attention scales linearly, so shells multiply cost, not profit.
